seo_title: Cost of Living in Chiang Mai 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Chiang Mai per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The world capital of digital nomads: low prices, a mild mountain climate, dozens of coworkings and an active international community. Ideal for those who work remotely and value a calm pace of life.
pros: The world capital of digital nomads, with dozens of coworkings
Low prices: housing, food and transport 2–3 times cheaper than Moscow
A mild mountain climate — cooler than Phuket
A large international community and a developed remote-work infrastructure
Close to nature: mountains, waterfalls, temples and elephant sanctuaries
cons: The Burning Season from February to April brings heavy air pollution
The rainy season runs from June to October
Getting around is inconvenient without a motorbike or car
Difficulties with international payments and Russian cards

best_places.name: Nimmanhaemin
best_places.description: A hipster district with dozens of cafés, bars, boutiques and coworkings.

best_places.name: Punspace
best_places.description: Chiang Mai's main coworking chain — an iconic spot among nomads.

best_places.name: Old City

best_places.name: Doi Suthep
best_places.description: The city's main temple on the mountain, with a panoramic view over Chiang Mai.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 60 days without a visa on a passport, with a 30-day extension at immigration.

visa_steps.title: Education Visa or DTV
visa_steps.description: A study visa (Thai language, Muay Thai) or the DTV for nomads — a year or more of stay.

visa_steps.title: Tax ID (TIN)
visa_steps.description: Needed for a bank account and a long-term lease — issued at the Revenue Department.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Kasikorn, SCB, Bangkok Bank — open accounts with a visa and a lease contract.

visa_steps.title: Renting a home
visa_steps.description: Contracts from 6 months; in the Old City and Nimman prices are lower than in Bangkok or Phuket.

faq.question: What is the Burning Season in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: February–April — farmers burn their fields and the air becomes hazardous (AQI 200+). Many nomads leave during this period.

faq.question: When is the best season in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: November–January — dry and cool (+20–28°C), perfect for living and working.

faq.question: How is banking in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: Kasikorn and SCB open accounts for Russians with a visa and a contract, but VISA cards are issued selectively.

faq.question: Can I relocate with children to Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: Yes, there are many international schools (CMIS, Lanna, Prem) and a strong parents' community.

faq.question: What about transport in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: Most people rent a motorbike (3,000–5,000 ₽/month); there's also Grab and songthaews (shared trucks).

faq.question: How is the internet in Chiang Mai?
faq.answer: Fibre at 300+ Mbps for 1,100–1,900 ₽, 4G/5G everywhere — one of the best cities for remote work.

reviews.text: Chiang Mai is for those who want to work remotely and spend little. The downside is the Burning Season — I fly to Bali for two months.
I rented a studio in Nimman for 28,000 ₽ and go to the Punspace coworking. Quiet, safe, affordable and lots of nomad friends.
